one_liner: Rust SIMD CRC library with a C ABI, covering every catalogued CRC-16/32/64 variant plus custom parameters; beats table-driven CRC crates.
what_it_does: Computes any Rocksoft-model CRC-16, CRC-32 or CRC-64, including all reveng-catalogued variants, forward (non-reflected) ones and user-defined parameters, using carry-less-multiply SIMD folding instead of lookup tables. The API has one-shot `checksum(CrcAlgorithm, &[u8]) -> u64`, specialized helpers (`crc32_iscsi`, `crc32_iso_hdlc`, `crc64_nvme`), a streaming `Digest` (implements `digest::DynDigest` and `std::io::Write`), `checksum_file`, `checksum_combine` and `*_with_params` variants. `cargo build` also emits a cdylib, a staticlib and an auto-generated `libcrc_fast.h` for C/C++ or other FFI callers. It is not a drop-in for the `crc` crate's `Crc<T>` API.
how_it_is_fast: Uses PCLMULQDQ/PMULL polynomial folding from Intel's 'Fast CRC Computation for Generic Polynomials Using PCLMULQDQ' paper, folding 8 blocks at a time rather than 4, with per-algorithm fold constants. That makes one kernel work for any polynomial, including forward CRCs, which pay an extra byte-shuffle. On x86_64 it widens to 512-bit VPCLMULQDQ with AVX-512 ternary XOR, and on aarch64 it uses the SHA3 EOR3 three-way XOR. For CRC-32C (x86 and aarch64) and CRC-32/ISO-HDLC (aarch64 only), it 'fuses' SIMD CLMUL folding with the native CRC32 instructions (corsix/dougallj technique). The kernel is chosen once at runtime from CPUID/HWCAP and cached in a OnceLock.
when_to_use: You need a CRC variant other than plain CRC-32 accelerated: CRC-64/NVME (the AWS S3 checksum), CRC-64/XZ or ECMA-182, CRC-32/BZIP2 or MPEG-2, CRC-16 protocols, or a custom polynomial via `CrcParams`.
Bulk checksumming of buffers 1 KiB and up on AVX-512 + VPCLMULQDQ servers (Sapphire Rapids, Genoa) or Apple M3/M4 and Graviton4 with SHA3, where the published 1 MiB rates are about 54-111 GiB/s.
Parallel or distributed checksumming where per-chunk CRCs are merged with `checksum_combine` (for example multipart uploads).
C, C++ or PHP code that wants one prebuilt shared or static library covering many CRC variants instead of vendoring per-variant kernels.
when_not_to_use: x86_64 CPUs with VPCLMULQDQ but no AVX-512 (Zen 3, Alder Lake to Meteor Lake clients, Sierra Forest) fall back to the 128-bit SSE PCLMULQDQ kernel. An AVX2 tier is only an open PR (#56), so the headline numbers do not apply there.

no_std on x86_64: 1.10.0 fails to compile because avx512.rs imports `std::arch` (issue #57; the fix, PR #42, is unmerged). no_std builds also have no runtime CPU detection and use only compile-time target features.

Workloads that combine many checksums in a hot loop: `checksum_combine` is slow (issue #59 measured 13.6 ms for 256 CRC-64 combines; PR #60 reports about 125 us per combine at 1 MiB length on Zen 3). Precomputation fixes are open, not merged.

Small messages (<1 KiB): no published numbers below 1 KiB. On x86 the CRC-32/ISO-HDLC 1 KiB rate (~28 GiB/s on SPR) is well under half the 1 MiB rate because there is no native instruction to fuse with.

If you need prompt dependency and security maintenance: no commits since 2025-12-27, a yanked `spin` 0.10.0 dependency (#53) and 2026 dependency-bump PRs are unaddressed, and a contributor has started a fork, calling the author inactive.

integration.form: crate (also builds cdylib + staticlib with generated C header libcrc_fast.h)
integration.dependencies: spin 0.10 (on x86/x86_64/aarch64); digest 0.10 (pulled in by the default std/alloc features); hashbrown 0.16 only with the `cache` feature
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.89 for 1.10.0 (1.9.x and earlier: Rust 1.81); stated MSRV policy is stable minus 2
integration.platforms: x86_64 (SSE4.1+PCLMULQDQ baseline, AVX-512VL+VPCLMULQDQ fast path), x86 (SSE PCLMULQDQ), aarch64 (PMULL; SHA3/EOR3 preferred); table fallback elsewhere, tested on wasm32, Cortex-M and RISC-V32
integration.thread_safety: Not explicitly documented. The functions are pure; CPU dispatch is initialized once via std OnceLock (spin::Once in no_std); `Digest` is a plain Copy value with no shared state; the FFI error status is thread-local.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — `crc32_iso_hdlc(&[u8]) -> u32` matches crc32fast::hash and the crc crate's CRC_32_ISO_HDLC output, but the streaming `Digest` (u64 finalize, algorithm enum) differs from both crc32fast::Hasher and crc's Crc<u32>/Digest API

gotchas: `checksum()` and `Digest::finalize()` return u64 for every width, so CRC-16/32 results need a cast.

The C API returns 0 on error (null pointer, bad params, file I/O failure), and 0 is also a valid CRC, so check `crc_fast_get_last_error()`, which is thread-local. The header's error enum constants are unprefixed (`Success`, `NullPointer`, ...) and can collide in C.

Default features include `ffi` and `panic-handler`. no_std binaries must set default-features = false, or they get the crate's `loop {}` panic handler and, with alloc, a stub global allocator that always returns null.
Uses a lot of `unsafe` intrinsics (checked with Miri on x86_64 and libFuzzer). 1.4.0 raised SIGILL on non-AVX-512 CPUs, including via aws-sdk-s3 (issue #14, fixed in 1.4.1), so require >=1.4.1.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over crc32fast when you need anything besides CRC-32/ISO-HDLC (CRC-32C, CRC-64/NVME, forward or custom CRCs), or a C ABI. For plain CRC-32 on AVX2-only VPCLMULQDQ x86, crc32fast 1.5.1+ has a 256-bit path that crc-fast lacks. Pick it over corsix fast-crc32 or htot crc32c when you want one runtime-dispatched package for many variants rather than C source kernels for CRC-32/CRC-32C only, which crc-fast's fusion paths borrow from.
verified_claims_summary: The author's own Criterion runs (random 1 KiB and 1 MiB buffers, release profile with LTO, rustc version not stated) give about 111 GiB/s CRC-32/ISCSI and about 88 GiB/s CRC-32/ISO-HDLC at 1 MiB on an EC2 c7i metal Sapphire Rapids using the AVX-512 VPCLMULQDQ path, and about 94-99 GiB/s on Apple M3 Ultra/M4 Max. The '>220X' figure divides these by a one-line '~0.5 GiB/s' claim for the `crc` crate that the repo never benchmarks, on unstated hardware. The README's link to that section points to a heading that does not exist.
status_note: Widely deployed (about 56M crates.io downloads; reverse deps include aws-smithy-checksums, object_store and uucore) and dual MIT/Apache-2.0, though src/combine.rs carries Mark Adler's zlib-licensed code (PR #41). It counts as active under the 12-month rule, but there have been no commits since the 1.10.0 release on 2025-12-27, and 2026 issues and fix PRs are unanswered.
